meta.move: Skilled teacher reaches the deal, asks 'Do we have an agreement?', then sends END MEETING
meta.expect: END MEETING gets FOLLOW-UP EMAIL and DEBRIEF at once

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, and why did he find out on his phone?
Thanks for coming in. The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent, so the zero stands.
A machine's guess, and Turnitin's own guide says not to use it as the sole basis for punishing a student. Your own procedure says the same thing, at 4.3. So what else do you have?
Let me start again. I entered the zero before I called you. Our procedure says I should have called first. That was wrong, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone in class.
Okay.

The checker score is the weakest thing I have, and it isn't why I'm concerned. I've turned my screen to you. This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of font, name and spacing changes. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. Kids draft in one place and paste into another, Hale, so a paste proves where it landed, not who wrote it. Was Owen asked about any of this before the zero went in?

If he wrote it over the weekend in another document, he can show us that document and its history, and I'll look at it gladly. Second thing. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." Here's the play open to that scene. That line is not in Hamlet. Look for it yourself.
Turn the play to me. A seventeen-year-old misremembers a line, and a bad quotation makes him careless, not a fraud. If he has the weekend draft, he'll show it.
Third. On October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing that Hamlet delays out of cowardice. Here's the outline. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and a final draft, Hale. And you went past the quotation: a misremembered line is a careless kid.

Fourth. On November 2 I asked Owen about his essay for five minutes. My notes written that day say that when I asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck", and he could not say which scene his second paragraph was about.
So he was asked, on November 2, and the zero went in the next day without a call to me. Five minutes, cornered by his teacher, and a kid goes blank. Show me the notes.

Fifth. His in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. Here it is beside the essay, which has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.

Forty minutes on a clock against a weekend with the play open, of course it's cleaner. You still haven't shown me those notes. Whatever comes next, Hale, nothing goes on his record and nobody in that class hears about it.

I'm not asking you to agree he did anything. Procedure 4.4 allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. It would be private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing to you tonight.
That's 4.4, in writing, tonight, and I'll take the rewrite to put this behind him. It happens this week, and the new mark is in before December 1. I still want your November 2 notes in that email.
I know his marks matter for his applications this semester. He can write it this Thursday after school, and I'll have it marked within two days.
Thursday after school. Who supervises him, and where?
So: a private supervised rewrite this Thursday, its mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, all in writing tonight. Do we have an agreement?
Yes, once that email names who supervises him and where, and has your November 2 notes attached. Thursday after school, marked within two days, nothing on his record.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite this Thursday after school, that it will be marked within two days, that its mark replaces the zero, and that nothing goes on his record. I still require that your email name who will supervise him and where, and that it attach your notes from November 2. I expect that email tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and accepted a private supervised rewrite this Thursday after school, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants your email to name the supervisor and the room and to attach your November 2 notes; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: You turned the screen and walked her through the version history with exact times, then answered her paste defence by inviting Owen to produce his weekend draft, because that was specific, dated, his own document, and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: You opened by leading with the checker's percentage and saying the zero stands, which handed her the argument she came prepared to win and kept her at her opening position.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placed the essay's whole creation between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM on the night before it was due, which came very close to that kind of late night, though it proves nothing about the essay and is simply why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked to see your November 2 notes, hand them across right then before moving on to the in-class writing, so that piece stands in the room instead of staying open into her email.
